claims.text: ADR 0019 @ stage-4 (Accepted): api gets a canary through the Gateway with the steps and limits of canary-checks.md; Notifications and Payments get rolling updates; changes customers see deploy behind a flag that is off; blue-green is rejected.

ADR 0019 context: per ADR 0012 every shop (1,000 planned) shares one deployment, so a broken release reaches every shop at once; api gets requests through the Gateway (HTTPRoute api), Notifications only messages from RabbitMQ, Payments saga messages plus route /api/v1/refunds for staff.

ADR 0019 options: blue-green runs a second full set of api Pods, doubling api Pods and the PostgreSQL connections capacity-plan.md counts for api; a canary adds one small api-canary Deployment and goes back by setting its weight to 0, as quickly as blue-green.
HTTPRoute backendRefs weights split only the requests that match that route's rule; traffic that does not pass through the Gateway, such as messages a Pod reads from a queue, is not affected by them.
claims.source_hint: Gateway API docs: HTTPRoute spec, BackendRef weight; Traffic splitting guide

claims.text: When several consumers read one RabbitMQ queue, each message is delivered to one of them; the broker does not choose by application version, so during a rolling update old and new Pods both take messages from the queue.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs: Consumers (multiple consumers on a queue, round-robin delivery); ADR 0019 lines 41-43 @ stage-4

claims.text: During a rolling update old and new Pods run together and the new share grows one step of Pods at a time; api.yaml sets no strategy, so default maxSurge 25% rounded up gives one extra Pod for 2 or 3 replicas: the smallest step is a whole Pod of requests. Going back is another rollout.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Deployments > Rolling Update Deployment, Max Surge (default 25%, rounded up); Rolling Back a Deployment; deploy api.yaml (no strategy) @ stage-4; ADR 0019 lines 11-13

claims.text: ADR 0019: Payments' route /api/v1/refunds gets few requests and its main work comes through the queue, so the team builds no separate canary for it; lines 74-77: blue-green for Payments would not separate queue work because both sets of Pods read one queue.

ADR 0019 consequences: each release keeps a schema the previous release's code runs on; in a canary one customer can meet both versions in one session; each reads what the other writes; so any release is undone by redeploying the previous one; messages likewise both ways.

ADR 0019 lines 59-61 + slo.md policy lines 92-94: when a service's budget is spent its feature releases stop and only fixes ship until its SLI is back above the SLO; an api fix still goes through every canary step. slo.md does not say whether a deploy behind a flag at 0 counts.

canary-checks.md: steps 10/50/100; each canary 5xx counts in the api's error budget, so stopping early spends only the canary's failed requests; a fix still goes all three steps because a broken fix would spend more of a spent budget.

ADR 0019 reopen conditions: a shop needs its own deployment (reopens ADR 0012 too); a change cannot be made compatible with the previous release; Notifications or Payments start getting most of their work through the Gateway.
slo.md: every SLI is measured at DonHang.Api; S1 is order placement without 5xx on POST api/v1/orders and api/v2/orders.
A breaking message shape can be published under a new routing key beside the old one until every reader has moved (expand and contract for messages).
Opinion: choose a release strategy per component by how its work arrives, when components differ in that; one shared rule fails for some components or falls to the weakest option for all.

Opinion: when a release cannot be made compatible, reopen the ADR before that release rather than during it; when a service starts getting most work through the Gateway, give it a canary with steps written before its first release.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0019 reopen conditions; canary-checks.md lines 4-6 (limits written before the release)

claims.text: Opinion: an urgent api fix should still take every canary step when the system is one shared deployment, because a broken fix reaches every shop at once.

DonHang.Api also reads payment events from queue orders.payment-events (PaymentEventsConsumer); api-canary runs the same image with the same RabbitMQ settings, so it takes those events from its first minute; the route weight caps only its HTTP share.

claims.text: ADR 0019 lines 62-63: staging gets Prometheus to count requests per Deployment, and labels api-canary and api-green in NetworkPolicies that list api; api-green is the green Deployment of the blue-green lab, deploy/gitops/lessons/api-green.yaml, present at stage-4.
Opinion: while slo.md is silent on whether a deploy behind a flag set to 0 counts as a feature release, hold that deploy too when the service's budget is spent.
